headline: Congress approved specified amendments to a US-UK agreement on atomic energy for mutual defense, treating them as having met the usual congressional review requirements.
what_it_does: The law lets certain amendments to the 1958-era US-UK agreement on sharing atomic energy for defense purposes take effect without the normal congressional review steps that the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 would require. Once those amendments take effect, they are subject to the Atomic Energy Act and other applicable US laws, as if they had gone through that review. The summary does not list the specific changes made by the amendments.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that carry out nuclear defense cooperation with the United Kingdom
who_it_affects.how: The amended agreement sets the terms under which these agencies may cooperate with the UK on defense uses of atomic energy.

when_it_takes_effect: The approval took effect when the law was enacted on December 16, 2014, and the amendments take effect under their own terms after that.
